article.articleSummary:
- Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused more than 4,000 deaths, with nearly 8,300 confirmed cases across seven provinces as of 2026-10-03. The outbreak records 8,300 cases and 4,018 fatalities, a case-fatality rate of 48.4%, with about 2,162 recoveries. Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya warns Ebola poses a threat to neighboring countries. The figures come from Actualite, citing the National Institute for Public Health in Congo (INSP). The report, relayed by Sputnik via ANTARA, notes ongoing transmission across seven provinces and highlights cross-border risk, though it provides no symptom detail or laboratory confirmation specifics.
- Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has killed 4,018 people and infected 8,300, according to Health Ministry figures released on Thursday. The authorities characterize this as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history, with ongoing transmission across the DRC challenging containment. The situation is further strained by reports that health workers are fighting to receive pay, potentially affecting the response. These figures—4,018 deaths among 8,300 cases—represent the latest update from the Health Ministry as authorities continue efforts to control transmission in affected regions.
- In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ebola virus disease outbreak has become the country’s deadliest on record, now surpassing 4,000 deaths. According to Congolese authorities, the death toll crossed the 4,000 threshold as of Friday, October 2, 2026. The update underscores the sustained severity of the outbreak in the DRC, with authorities providing current tallies on the evolving situation. The article highlights the scale of the epidemic in the DRC and marks a grim milestone in the country’s long history with Ebola, reflecting a public health emergency of significant magnitude.

The United Nations warned that the challenge of stopping Ebola transmission in the DRC is becoming harder. A transit center for Ebola at Kigonze was burned down this week, hampering outbreak containment. The facility, run by the International Medical Corps and supported by more than 50 staff, was used to isolate and screen suspected cases before patients were moved on for care. article.articleHeadline: Ferdi Sambo and 500 Cibinong Prison inmates undergo health checks, with hypertension and scabies.
article.articleSummary: At Lapas Kelas IIA Cibinong, Bogor Regency, Indonesia, 500 inmates underwent free health screening as part of the GOTD Limitless – Love Without Limits social service on Oct 2, 2026. Ferdy Sambo was among participants, receiving medical evaluation and laboratory tests. Screening proceeded with registration, blood pressure measurement, and general health checks, followed by laboratory tests as indicated. Dr. Yenny Chandrawaty reported a high prevalence of scabies among inmates, prompting hygiene education and guidance on sun-drying bedding to reduce mite transmission. Medications were provided free when needed, alongside education on clean-living practices. Sambo’s lab results showed normal glucose, uric acid, and cholesterol, but a somewhat elevated blood pressure. The event emphasized preventive care and health education for prisoners, with patient-centered screening and free access to medications. Keywords: infectious disease, scabies, outbreak prevention, prison health.

article.articleHeadline: Pertamina Hospital Balikpapan Doctor Reveals Vulnerable Groups at Risk of Influenza
article.articleSummary: Influenza is a viral disease caused by diverse influenza viruses, with presentations that can be seasonal or occur year-round. In Balikpapan, East Kalimantan, Indonesia, Dr. Rony Kharisma, a general practitioner and head of the OHIH at Pertamina Balikpapan Hospital, says all ages are at risk, though children and the elderly are more susceptible to influenza-related respiratory complications due to developing lungs and aging physiology. The public is urged to remain vigilant as respiratory disturbances rise in the surrounding environment. Poor air quality, including haze from smoke, can exacerbate risks, as airborne particles may contribute to influenza. The discussion, reported on October 2, 2026, emphasizes environmental health and targeted protection for vulnerable populations, without citing specific case counts or laboratory confirmations.

article.articleHeadline: Nine Years of Insurance Data Reveal Indonesia's Stubborn Typhoid
article.articleSummary: Typhoid fever remains a high-burden public health problem in Indonesia, based on BPJS Kesehatan data from 2015–2023 covering about 8 million encounters among ~6.9 million individuals in all provinces. With 95.9% population coverage in 2023, the dataset offers a national view of typhoid-related healthcare utilization in primary care and hospitals. Peak annual prevalence reached 347 per 100,000 in primary care (2017) and 314 per 100,000 in hospitals (2016); by 2023, estimates were 143 per 100,000 in primary care and 167 per 100,000 in hospitals, still above the high-burden threshold of 100 per 100,000. Hospital admissions accounted for 47.6% of visits; cumulative hospital deaths reached 11,991, averaging 0.57 deaths per 100,000 per year. Diagnoses relied on physician ICD-10 coding (A01.0) rather than routine microbiological confirmation; Widal/rapid tests are commonly used, with culture confirmation rare. Burden skewed toward young children; subsidised low-income enrollees had higher hospitalization risk; pronounced subnational clustering observed.

article.articleHeadline: Jakarta: No. 2 in TB Cases — Is Population Density the Cause?
article.articleSummary: TB (Mycobacterium tuberculosis) in Indonesia is analyzed through population-density–based rankings, with Bangka Belitung first and Jakarta (DKI) second in TB case counts when viewed by density, prompting questions about the indicators used. Deputy Health Minister Dante Saksono Harbuwono notes that density can elevate airborne transmission but is not a direct measure of incidence. Absolute case counts, cases per 100,000 people, prevalence, and cases per area each yield different epidemiologic pictures; mixing indicators risks misinterpretation. In Jakarta, high urban mobility, housing density, poor ventilation, socioeconomic disparities, and cross-district movement complicate TB control; density alone does not capture risk. The article calls for granular mapping by subdistrict, housing conditions, vulnerable groups, and testing/treatment coverage, and insists that case finding must be followed by complete treatment and ongoing patient support. Cross-regional comparisons require careful interpretation of surveillance and access to care.

article.articleHeadline: RespiraTB, a creation by UII students, can monitor TB symptoms in real time.
article.articleSummary: RespiraTB, a wearable platform developed by Universitas Islam Indonesia (UII) students in Yogyakarta, provides real-time, non-invasive screening for tuberculosis (TB) by continuously monitoring breathing characteristics. The accelerometer/IMU-based device tracks chest-wall movement and work of breathing; data are processed on ESP32 with filtering and a threshold-based respiratory risk score, then transmitted to a mobile app via Firebase. It is intended as an initial screening tool, not a substitute for clinical diagnosis. Lab testing shows respiratory-rate accuracy of 96.28% versus manual counts, with a maximum deviation of one breath per minute; MPU6050 accuracy 92.08% against Esophageal Pressure Catheter, and ESP32-to-app transmission success 100% with an average 2.2 seconds. The team—Afwan Aditya Saputra, Huda Nur Ihsan Muhammad Akbar, Isfana Fatimah Darman—developed under Ali Parkhan and showcased at The 12th UTU Awards 2026. Initial markets cover West, East, and Central Java; TAM about Rp1.035 trillion/year; first-year sales 1,380 units at Rp950,000.

article.articleHeadline: 2,675 TB patients were found in West Sulawesi throughout 2026; 269 died.
article.articleSummary: Tuberculosis cases in West Sulawesi, Indonesia, reached 2,675 detected in 2026, with 269 deaths during treatment. The West Sulawesi Health Office (DKPPKB) uses cohort-based evaluation for TB management, noting treatment lasts at least six months. In the 2025 treatment cohort (patients starting in 2024), 3,895 began therapy and 3,358 were cured; 236 defaulted and 231 died. For 2026 (treatment period 2025), 3,942 began treatment and 3,268 completed; 269 died and 173 defaulted. Case-finding has fluctuated in recent years: 2020 estimated 4,445 cases, 2,264 found and 2,067 treated; 2021 2,409 found and 2,239 treated; 2022 2,939 found and 2,781 treated; 2024 found 4,089 and 3,895 started treatment. The data highlight a sustained TB burden in the region, underscoring ongoing needs for case finding and treatment adherence.

article.articleHeadline: COVID-19, Broccolo: "Expected recovery, the virus is now endemic."
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 is now endemic, with SARS-CoV-2 potentially causing one or two waves per year, not following strict influenza-like seasonality, according to Francesco Broccolo, clinical microbiologist at the University of Salento. Among the circulating variants are NB181 and XFG, both descended from the JN-1 lineage. Spike-protein mutations may help these strains evade antibodies and trigger new infections in previously exposed people, but there is no evidence of increased clinical severity; they spread more easily rather than being more dangerous. Rising case numbers are driven by school and workplace return, more time indoors, and waning immunity over months. In China, late July–early August positivity rose above 20% without imposing major hospital strain. Protection should focus on the vulnerable: test symptomatic individuals, limit contact with the vulnerable, ensure good ventilation, and sustain genomic surveillance and laboratory diagnostics beyond emergencies as an early warning system.

article.articleHeadline: October Disease Risk Forecast Released; Hunan Prioritizes Prevention and Control of These Diseases.
article.articleSummary: Hunan Province, China, released its October disease risk forecast, with a prevention index at level III (medium). Six priority areas are highlighted. Mosquito-borne diseases (Dengue fever and Chikungunya) carry a moderate risk as mosquitoes remain active; watch for fever, orbital pain, rash, and conjunctival injection, and control mosquitoes at home and outdoors. Dog bites pose a rabies risk; ensure pet vaccination, keep dogs leashed, and seek immediate care if bitten. Acute respiratory infections rise with temperature swings; symptoms include fever, sore throat, cough, and fatigue; recommendations include ventilation, masking in crowded places, hand hygiene, and vaccination for vulnerable groups. Wild mushroom poisoning is common in autumn; avoid picking or eating wild mushrooms, and preserve samples if poisoning occurs. Toxic plant/animal-origin foodborne illnesses and microbiological foodborne diseases are also flagged; avoid unknown wild edibles, practice safe food handling, and seek care for symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: Still Air, Falling Temperatures: Weather Patterns Drive Influenza Surges in
article.articleSummary: Influenza in Nanchang, Jiangxi Province, China, shows climate-linked surges. In 120,308 laboratory-confirmed cases from Jan 2023–Mar 2026, activity peaks in winter–spring under a monsoon climate. The 2025 incidence reached 837.36 per 100,000 with the peak in Week 49. Children aged 0–19 accounted for 76% of cases, with students the largest occupational group; Xihu and Honggutan districts bore the heaviest burden. About 89.64% of cases were diagnosed within two days of symptom onset, but delays were more common among those 60+ and among farmers. Weather variables were linked to incidence: average temperature was the most important predictor with a U-shaped relationship, followed by wind speed, cloud cover, and precipitation. Random Forest identified these as key drivers; DLNM modeled lagged effects. The study suggests wind speed may offer an early warning signal; vaccination ahead of winter–spring surges and targeted diagnostics for elderly and rural populations are advised.

article.articleHeadline: Return of COVID-19, Bassetti comments on the rise in cases: "Here's what's happening."
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 is rising again, with Santé publique France reporting a 76% increase in GP visits for COVID-19 during the week of 14–20 September (data updated 23 September). Matteo Bassetti, head of the Infectious Diseases Department at San Martino Hospital, attributes the resurgence to waning immunity from vaccination and prior infections, and notes reduced testing masking true case counts. He also observes that current presentations resemble influenza, with mild cold-like symptoms and headaches. The uptick has appeared in France, the United States, and China, and is now also emerging in Italy. While generally not severe for the broader population, the elderly and those with comorbidities over 80 should receive annual vaccination, as vaccines administered in 2021 offer little protection for this age group.

article.articleHeadline: Eating sushi, vomiting and diarrhea! Mass poisoning of 360 people in Sweden; Norovirus detected in a famous Korean seaweed snack.
article.articleSummary: Norovirus outbreak in Sweden linked to a Korean seaweed snack sickened about 360 people at two sushi restaurants in Laholm Municipality in April 2026, with vomiting and diarrhea as the main symptoms. Unopened sushi seaweed was tested, revealing norovirus with the same genotype as patients. The batch, produced by the Guangchuan Seaweed brand and imported from Korea, led to a nationwide recall of about 22,000 packs in May and immediate destruction of the affected stock. While the Swedish Food Agency noted the manufacturing date was roughly 10 months prior to the outbreak, attribution to the seaweed remains uncertain and other infection sources are possible. The Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety said the batch had been exported in July 2025, over a year before; the virus's infectiousness is considered unlikely, but monitoring continues. The episode raises European calls for stricter heavy metals and microbiological testing on seaweed products.

article.articleHeadline: Older Adults Delay Seeking Rabies Treatment After Animal Bites, Hangzhou
article.articleSummary: Rabies remains nearly 100% fatal after symptom onset but preventable with timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). A Hangzhou, China study of 3,327 exposure-related clinic visits (October 2022–October 2025) at Tongde Hospital of Zhejiang Province examined why people delay care. Only 218 visits (6.6%) occurred on a calendar day after injury, using calendar-day delay as a conservative proxy. After adjustment, patients aged 65 and older had significantly higher odds of delayed presentation than those 15–44 years (aOR 2.28; 95% CI 1.31–3.96; p=0.003). Pre-hospital wound self-treatment was associated with higher odds of delay (aOR 2.72; 95% CI 2.00–3.69). The oldest group was less likely to report self-treatment, but this was not statistically significant (aOR 0.71; 95% CI 0.50–1.01; p=0.056). Findings were modeled separately; no individual linkage between delay and self-care. Implication: targeted outreach in Hangzhou to prompt prompt PEP after bites. WHO guidelines stress washing wounds for at least 15 minutes.

article.articleHeadline: Asian Games / Taekwondo: Wang Weijia Infected with Norovirus Before Competition, Wins Bronze; Coach Unveils Unconventional Tactic, Joking That the Negative-Mindset Approach Works
article.articleSummary: Wang Weijia of Taiwan won bronze in the women’s 67 kg taekwondo at the Nagoya, Aichi 2026 Asian Games after contracting Norovirus a week before departure, severely limiting training. Coach Su Tai-yuan reported rapid recovery with medical help from Dr. Lin Sheng-zhang, and he credits an unconventional “negative mindset” motivational tactic—telling her she would lose—to spur a comeback, praising her resolve as “over 100 points.” In the event, Wang defeated China’s Xing Jianni in the quarterfinals before losing 3–14, 5–7 to Iran’s Saghar Moradi in the semifinals, earning Taiwan’s first taekwondo medal of the Games. This marked Wang’s first Asian Games appearance, following prior world championships and Universiade disappointments, and she expressed satisfaction with her performance despite not reaching the gold-medal match.

article.articleHeadline: Smart Early Warning System Sharpens Hospital Infection Surveillance, Study
article.articleSummary: In Guangzhou, China, at The Affiliated Guangdong Second Provincial General Hospital of Jinan University, a retrospective study evaluated an intelligent early warning system integrated with active surveillance for healthcare-associated infections (HAIs). The eight-year analysis compared pre-intervention (2018–2022) versus post-intervention (2023–2025) periods using interrupted time-series methods. The hospital identified 2,600 HAI cases in the pre period and 1,697 in the post period. Delayed reporting declined from 32.85% to 28.23% (p=0.001); time-series estimates showed a sustained quarterly drop of 1.240 percentage points (95% CI −2.408 to −0.078; p=0.033). Pre-discharge reporting rose from 74.54% to 89.69% (p<0.001), with an immediate level increase of 13.453 percentage points (CI 3.143–23.763; p=0.012). Median delays shortened: onset-to-discharge 11→9 days; reporting-to-discharge 9→7 days (both p<0.001). The findings support the value of combining intelligent analytics with active surveillance to accelerate detection, isolation, and care in hospital infection control.

article.articleHeadline: Adenovirus and Mycoplasma Leave Distinct Biomarker Fingerprints in
article.articleSummary: From Hangzhou Children's Hospital, China, a retrospective cohort of 6,093 pediatric admissions with acute respiratory tract infections (0–18 years) from Jan 5, 2023 to Jun 17, 2025 used a 13-target pharyngeal-swab panel (collapsed into 11 pathogen groups) and evaluated associations with inflammatory biomarkers (CRP ≥20 mg/L; PCT ≥0.5 ng/mL) and hospital stay ≥7 days. Of participants, 2,076 were panel-negative, 3,343 had a single pathogen, and 674 had multiple detections. Adenovirus detection doubled the odds of elevated biomarkers (CRP OR 2.19, 95% CI 1.63–2.96; PCT OR 1.93, 95% CI 1.34–2.77). Mycoplasma pneumoniae linked to lower PCT elevation (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.13–0.37) but strongly predicted longer hospitalization (OR 2.57 for ≥7 days; 2.50 in the 24h subset, 2.76 in the 48h subset). Co-detections increased odds of longer stay (OR 2.21, 95% CI 1.73–2.82). Limitations: retrospective design; cannot prove causality; potential confounders include treatment and illness severity. Published in BMC Infectious Diseases.

article.articleHeadline: WHO warns of the death toll from cholera.
article.articleSummary: Cholera mortality alarm: WHO reports 2025: 451,499 cholera cases and 7,870 deaths across 47 countries, the highest annual cholera deaths reported to WHO since 1999; true burden likely higher due to under-reporting. About 90% of cases and deaths are in seven countries: Angola, Bangladesh, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Nigeria, South Sudan, Sudan, and Yemen. Africa region experienced a 34% increase in cases and 58% increase in deaths versus 2024. More than 20% of cholera deaths occur outside healthcare facilities, signaling limited timely care. Global supply of oral cholera vaccine rose from about 30 million doses in 2022 to nearly 80 million in 2025. In addition, 2025 saw 21,526 suspected meningitis cases with 971 deaths in 24 African countries; and plague reports show 3,847 suspected cases and 423 deaths 2019–2025 across 10 countries. article.articleHeadline: Pandemics like COVID-19, a risk to be debated at a UDC meeting: "The danger is real."
article.articleSummary: At the University of A Coruña, the CITIC hosts a two-day EU ZOE Consortium meeting on zoonotic emergence through degraded and restored forest ecosystems (ZOE). Felix Drexler of Charité, Berlin, warns the danger is real, citing COVID-19 and hantavirus as warnings and noting zoonoses are rising due to human disturbance and livestock intensification. The project studies 'disturbance grades' and how habitat disruption—such as hotels in wild areas or large livestock facilities housing tens of thousands of animals—can upset pathogens in wildlife hosts like bats and rodents, enabling spillover. COVID-19 was highly transmissible but not very lethal; Ebola in Congo is a worse zoonosis. ZOE aims to prevent future pandemics and aid vaccine development, informing policy to protect ecosystems and avert outbreaks. Teams in Guatemala and Mexico contribute, with UDC's Adina Dumitru leading analyses of human impact on ecosystems.

article.articleHeadline: Island Pharmaceuticals starts Galidesivir production for Ebola emergency-use program | Stockhead
article.articleSummary: Galidesivir production underway for Ebola emergency-use program in Uganda under the WHO MEURI framework. A second 5 kg batch is planned by late November to support a broader Ebola strategy and a planned Marburg study in non-human primates under FDA Animal Rule pathway. MEURI enables emergency access to unproven interventions with prospective data collection on efficacy, safety and virology, potentially adding human evidence to existing preclinical/clinical data. Uganda’s MEURI follows the Aug 27 end of its outbreak; however, Bundibugyo in the DRC has reported 8,137 cases and 3,926 deaths as of Sept 27 (CFR ~48%).

article.articleSummary: Published 2026-10-02: Adventurer Ash Dykes launches Project Six, a month-long Congo Basin expedition down the Sangha River, paddling 434 miles on an inflatable kayak with a small team. article.articleHeadline: What Is Mpox (Monkeypox)?
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) is a viral disease with two clades: Congo Basin (up to 10% mortality) and West African (about 1% mortality; the 2022 outbreak). There is no mpox-specific approved treatment; antivirals developed for smallpox may help, usually reserved for immunocompromised patients: cidofovir, brincidovir (Tembexa), and tecovirimat (Tpoxx). Incubation is 5–21 days; initial flu-like symptoms (fever, headache, muscle aches, lymphadenopathy, fatigue) precede a rash that begins on the face and spreads to the hands and feet. Transmission occurs through close contact with infected people or animals, including respiratory secretions, lesions, or contaminated materials; animal exposure includes bites, scratches, meat, or products. Pregnant individuals can pass the virus to a fetus. Diagnosis relies on PCR from lesion samples. Vaccines: JYNNEOS (two-dose, approved 2019; up to 85% effective; effective within four days of exposure) and ACAM2000 (single-dose). Mpox is typically self-limiting in 14–21 days, though severe disease and complications can occur, especially in children.

triage.headline_ja: Mpox（サル痘）とは何か？
triage.triage_reason: 特定の発生事象を報じるニュースではなく、Mpoxの病態・症状・治療・ワクチンに関する一般的な解説記事であるため、トリアージ対象のシグナルに該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事はMpoxの病態・感染経路・治療法・ワクチンに関する一般教育的な解説記事であり、DRC・ナイジェリア・アンゴラ等での具体的な発生事例を報じるものではない。発生地域タグはBluedotによる誤分類の可能性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Exotic Pet Trade Poses Rising Zoonotic Disease Risks in India
article.articleSummary: India's exotic pet trade elevates zoonotic spillover risk as close contact with imported wild animals creates repeated opportunities for pathogens to jump to humans. In Mumbai, avian and exotic wildlife veterinarian Dr. Rina Dev treats imported animals and warns psittacosis (avian chlamydiosis) is a common risk for bird handlers. Traders can carry salmonellosis from reptiles and tuberculosis from primates, with tuberculosis increasingly detected among primates. Nonhuman primates can transmit Ebola and HIV to people, underscoring cross-species danger. Global analyses show traded mammals are 1.5 times more likely to share pathogens with humans than nontraded species, with roughly one additional shared pathogen per decade of trade. A 2026 Humane World for Animals report notes 75% of emerging infectious diseases are zoonotic and estimates about 850,000 unknown viruses in birds and mammals that could infect people. Risks rise in pet cafes, petting zoos, and public events; first responders often lack PPE, and illegal trafficking bypasses quarantine. A One Health approach is urged, but investment remains limited.

triage.headline_ja: エキゾチックペット取引がインドで高まる人獣共通感染症リスクをもたらす
triage.triage_reason: 具体的な発生事例や症例数の報告ではなく、エキゾチックペット取引に伴う人獣共通感染症リスクに関する一般的な解説・啓発記事であるため、シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。
triage.notes: 具体的な感染症アウトブレイクの報告ではなく、エキゾチックペット取引による人獣共通感染症リスク全般についての解説記事。複数疾患（オウム病、結核、エボラ、HIV）が言及されているが、いずれも具体的な発生事例ではなく潜在的リスクの説明にとどまる。

article.articleHeadline: Deadly Brain Infection From Soil Bacteria Exposed by Tamil Nadu Outbreak
article.articleSummary: Neuromelioidosis, a rare brain/spinal cord infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, is highlighted by a southern India focus. Global melioidosis estimates reach about 165,000 cases and 89,000 deaths annually; neurological involvement is typically 2–5% but regional data from southern India show higher proportions. In 2022–2023, a northern Tamil Nadu outbreak documented 22 probable cases across four districts with eight deaths, linked to contaminated saline used in a dental-care setting, revealing healthcare-associated transmission. Whole-genome sequencing identified sequence type ST1553; the bimA Bm allele appeared in three clonal isolates (two clinical, one from saline), with core-SNP phylogeny supporting a common source. Burkholderia pseudomallei displays diverse lineages; bimA Bm is associated with neurotropism but is not a standalone predictor. A standardized core-genome MLST scheme (4,221 targets) underpins international molecular surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: タミル・ナードゥ州の発生事例で明らかになった土壌細菌による致死的な脳感染症
triage.triage_reason: 2022-2023年に発生したタミル・ナードゥ州の神経メリオイドーシス集団感染（歯科医療関連、汚染生理食塩水が原因）に関する遡及的・科学的な分析記事であり、既に原因特定・制御済みで現在進行中の伝播リスクは低いため、新規シグナルとしての緊急性は限定的と判断。
triage.notes: 記事は2022-2023年に発生し既に原因（歯科施設での汚染生理食塩水）が特定・制御済みの集団感染についてのゲノム解析を含む学術的報告であり、現在進行中の新規アウトブレイクではない。メリオイドーシスはヒト-ヒト感染しない土壌由来細菌感染症であり、国際的拡大リスクは低い。続報や新規症例の有無を注視する。

article.articleHeadline: A month-long awareness campaign to prevent communicable diseases.
article.articleSummary: Kushinagar, Uttar Pradesh hosts a month-long awareness campaign by the Agriculture Department addressing infectious diseases spread by rats and shrews. The campaign warns that flooded fields drive rodents toward homes, increasing risks of Scrub Typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi) and Leptospirosis (Leptospira). Symptoms include high fever, headache, severe muscle pain, calf pain, and red eyes. To mitigate risk, authorities advocate rodent control with baits, using Zinc Phosphide 80% WP under expert guidance; Aluminum Phosphide is highly toxic and must follow safety standards and expert advice; Bromadiolone 0.005% bait should be used in prescribed amounts. Keep poisons away from children and non-targets. Preserve natural predators such as cats, snakes, owls, foxes, and hawks. Emphasize sanitation, cover and securely store food, and seek immediate medical care for fever, headache, or red eyes.

triage.headline_ja: 感染症予防のための1か月間の啓発キャンペーン
triage.triage_reason: 啓発活動に関する予防的な広報記事であり、具体的な症例数・流行発生の報告がなく、IHR・WPRO基準のいずれにも該当しない。
triage.notes: 本記事は実際の発生事例報告ではなく、農業局によるネズミ媒介感染症（ツツガムシ病・レプトスピラ症）の予防啓発キャンペーンを伝えるもの。具体的な感染者数や流行状況の記載がないため対象国としては計上せず。

article.articleHeadline: In Sangamner, a ring of muddy water! Hospitals filled with infectious diseases; questions raised about the administration's statistics.
article.articleSummary: Sangamner city confronts a mud-filled water crisis as taps deliver turbid drinking water, with sediments seen after storage. Despite dam releases from Bhandardara, Nilwande, and Adhala, clean water remains scarce. A drought year (rainfall about 50% of last year) worsens the situation, though certain floods temporarily filled reservoirs. Hospitals report rising cases of fever, cold, cough, body aches, abdominal and back pain, along with dengue, malaria, chikungunya, and jaundice. In September 2026, dengue testing covered 73 samples with 8 positives; chikungunya had 4 samples tested with none positive; malaria had 9,149 samples tested with none positive. A month recorded eight dengue cases. Government data versus private hospitals show substantial discrepancies in patient counts, prompting questions about surveillance. Routine fumigation is reportedly not being conducted, compounding public health risk amid ongoing outbreaks and water contamination concerns.

triage.headline_ja: サンガムネルで濁水問題！病院は感染症患者で溢れる──行政統計に疑問の声
triage.triage_reason: インド・マハラシュトラ州サンガムネル市で水質汚染に伴うデング熱・マラリア・チクングニア等の症例増加が報告されているが、規模は小規模で重症度や国際的拡大の情報がなく、続報を注視すべき段階。
triage.notes: パキスタン（Punjab州等）の地域情報が付与されているが、記事本文はインド・マハラシュトラ州サンガムネル市の水質汚染と感染症流行に限定されており、パキスタンは主題に含まれないため除外した。症例数は小規模（デング8例陽性/73検体等）で、行政統計と民間病院データの乖離が指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: New COVID Wave in the US and the UK: The coronavirus has returned! Cases rising in Britain and America.
article.articleSummary: New COVID-19 wave is spreading in the United States and United Kingdom as Stratus (XFG), the so‑called American Covid strain first detected in January 2025, circulates in both countries. UK Health Security Agency data show weekly Covid hospital admissions rising from 0.81 to 1.20 per 100,000, with the share of positive tests increasing from 5.9% to 7%. In London, hospital admissions over seven days rose about 80%, and among those aged 85+ the rate increased from 7.08 to 12.43 per 100,000. Testing is not widespread, so the true scale may be higher. Symptoms resemble flu: sore throat, headache, runny nose, fatigue, with some patients reporting loss of taste and, in others, stomach/digestive issues. Dr. Rene Hoenderkamp notes recent patients with these symptoms, highlighting flu‑like illness linked to Stratus and potential winter co-circulation with other respiratory viruses.

triage.headline_ja: 米国と英国で新たなCOVIDの波：コロナウイルスが再来！イギリスとアメリカで感染者増加
triage.triage_reason: 英米でのCOVID新系統（Stratus/XFG）による入院増加が報告されているが、インドへの直接的な影響は見出しの疑問形に留まり、重症度や国際的拡大の具体的証拠が不足しているため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事は米国・英国でのCOVID-19新系統Stratus(XFG)の流行拡大を報じており、インドは見出しで言及されるのみで実際の感染拡大事例は記載されていない。対象国リストに米国・英国は含まれず、インドも感染発生国として確認できないためverified_locationsは空とする。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue outbreak in a densely populated area, eight more patients found.
article.articleSummary: Dengue outbreak expands in Kanpur, with eight new dengue cases reported in densely populated neighborhoods as of 2 October 2026. In Yashoda Nagar, a 16-year-old girl; in Parade area, a 29-year-old man; in Kalyanpur, a 35-year-old man; and in Gujaini, a 33-year-old man tested positive. The Medical College’s laboratory confirmed four additional dengue infections, all residents of crowded city areas. A separate scrub typhus case has also been identified, indicating concurrent vector-borne disease activity in Kanpur. The report highlights ongoing urban transmission in the city’s populous localities, but provides limited details on symptoms, exposure sources, clinical outcomes, or travel-related import/export status. Authorities are monitoring clusters and emphasizing targeted public health measures in high-density neighborhoods.

triage.headline_ja: 人口密集地域でデング熱アウトブレイク拡大、新たに8人の患者確認
triage.triage_reason: カンプールでのデング熱症例増加と散発的なツツガムシ病症例が報告されているが、重症度や感染源、国際的拡大の情報が不足しており、季節性の地域流行の可能性が高いため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: デング熱はインドでは毎年季節性に発生する風土病であり、本件は局地的な都市部クラスターとみられる。重症度・死亡例・ヒト-ヒト感染拡大の明確な情報がなく、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Physical Relations With Female Tenant, 2 Cousins Die After Testing HIV Positive in Bijnor; Panic Grips Area: What Happened?
article.articleSummary: As of 2 October 2026, two cousins in Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh, tested HIV-positive and subsequently died — the elder after failing to breathe on oxygen; the younger on Wednesday night. They had been ill for some time and were treated locally before hospitalization in Bijnor, Rishikesh, and Dehradun, where HIV infection was laboratory-confirmed. A local woman who had lived in the area is mentioned as a possible contact, but officials have not confirmed any transmission link. Relatives say the elder spoke of contact with the woman and that his cousin visited her rented room; the woman’s identity and HIV status remain undisclosed. Health authorities stress that two infections do not prove a transmission chain and that medical records and investigations are required. Further findings are awaited.

triage.headline_ja: 女性入居者との肉体関係、ビジュノールでHIV陽性と判明した従兄弟2人が死亡 ― 地域に恐怖広がる：何が起きたのか？
triage.triage_reason: 個別のHIV感染・死亡例であり、感染経路も未確認で公衆衛生上の緊急性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。地域住民の不安はあるが行政・国際的関心は低い。
triage.notes: HIVは既知の感染症であり、本件は個別死亡例の報道。感染経路は未確認で、当局も伝播連鎖を断定していない。地域内の噂・パニックに関する人間ドラマ的報道であり、アウトブレイクシグナルとしての要件を満たさない。

article.articleHeadline: Pilibhit News: Three chickenpox cases detected in the district jail spark panic; all inmates screened.
article.articleSummary: Three chickenpox cases confirmed in Pilibhit district jail, triggering screening of all inmates. The health department reports all inmates and detainees screened; so far no transmission detected outside those three. Four days earlier, one prisoner deteriorated with convulsions and fever; admitted to the jail hospital, then referred to Meerut Medical College due to limited facilities there. The next day, two more inmates developed chickenpox; all three were moved to Meerut for treatment. A jail health team reviewed the inmates' histories. All contacts have been tested. WHO has been asked to file a report. Surveillance has been stepped up; teams are active in flood-affected areas where similar infections have occurred in the past. The jail hospital doctors have been instructed to remain alert as investigations continue.

triage.headline_ja: ピリビート刑務所で水痘3例確認、全受刑者をスクリーニング実施
triage.triage_reason: 刑務所内という閉鎖空間での水痘集団発生だが、感染拡大は3例にとどまり国外拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低い。続報での感染拡大有無を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 水痘（Varicella）は一般的にIHR通報対象ではないが、閉鎖施設での集団発生のため地域保健当局の監視対象として要経過観察とした。WHOへの報告要請が記載されているが、これは地方当局の手続き上の対応と見られ、国際的な公衆衛生緊急事態としての性質は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Genetic Typing of Tuberculosis Isolates in Kerala Reveals Rare BCG Disease
article.articleSummary: In Kerala, India, a retrospective study of 239 MTBC isolates (2017–2024) using gyrB PCR-RFLP and RD1/RD4 markers finds 232 (97.1%) M. tuberculosis and 7 (2.9%) M. bovis BCG. No wild-type M. bovis or M. orygis detected. Four BCG isolates come from vaccinated children (including disseminated disease in some cases) and three from adults receiving intravesical BCG therapy for bladder cancer, highlighting that BCG infection can occur in both vaccination and therapy contexts. M. bovis BCG is naturally resistant to pyrazinamide, impacting standard four-drug regimens and treatment duration. This marks the first species-level MTBC map for Kerala, suggesting human-to-human transmission dominates locally with no zoonotic MTBC detected in this cohort. The approach—PCR-RFLP of gyrB plus RD1/RD4 assays—provides rapid, cost-effective speciation with important implications for laboratory workflows and clinical management in tuberculosis care and public health surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: ケララ州における結核分離株の遺伝子型解析により稀なBCG感染症例が明らかに
triage.triage_reason: 過去8年分の後方視的な分子疫学研究であり、新規アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の緊急対応を要する事象ではないため。
triage.notes: 本記事は2017-2024年の過去データを用いた遺伝子型別研究報告であり、現在進行中のアウトブレイクや新規感染事例の急増を示すものではない。

article.articleHeadline: Collector appeals to people to stop breeding of dengue-causing mosquitos at grama sabha meeting
article.articleSummary: On 2 October 2026, Virudhunagar Collector Sharanya Ari addressed a grama sabha at Vadamalakurichi in Virudhunagar union, Tamil Nadu, urging residents to curb dengue by preventing Aedes mosquito breeding in stagnant rainwater and discarded items. She emphasized removing water-collecting articles and promoting waste segregation to ease door-to-door collection and protect the environment. Dengue prevention was framed within broader governance, with mentions of welfare schemes and infrastructure needs, including upgrading the Government High School to a higher secondary, a bus shelter, protected drinking water, and sewerage cleaning, with commitments to pursue these requests. The meeting reviewed Panchayat expenditure from April 1 to September 30 and included an AIDS awareness pledge. Attendees included Project Director (DRDA) Vanathi, Joint Director of Agriculture Mohandoss Sowmiyan, Deputy Director of Horticulture A. Arumugam, Assistant Director (Panchayats) Muruganandam, and Sattur Revenue Divisional Officer Kanagarajan.

triage.headline_ja: 行政官、村落総会でデング熱媒介蚊の発生防止を住民に呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 通常の予防啓発活動を伝える行政広報的な記事であり、具体的な症例数や流行拡大の情報がなく、IHR・WPROいずれの基準にも該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事は蚊媒介病予防の地域啓発活動を報じるものであり、デング熱の流行状況や症例数についての具体的情報は含まれていない。

article.articleHeadline: Mysterious death of the 'Prince' in the jungle! No injuries on the body, no food found in the stomach... Which disease is making the ferocious animal ill?
article.articleSummary: Barwani, Madhya Pradesh: A two-year-old female tiger was found dead in Barwani Forest Division, near Rehgun village, about 200 metres into the jungle, around 6:35 pm. A postmortem led by Dr. Mahendra Baghel found no external injuries; the carcass had languished for about 48 hours. The abdomen contained neither food nor water, and lesions were noted in the stomach suggesting possible infection. Doctors cite dehydration and infection as potential drivers; septicemia remains a concern but the exact cause awaits laboratory confirmation on viscera samples. Poison was not indicated. This is the second tiger death in West Nimad within a short span; earlier, on Sept 11, an adult tiger in Chirai Forest range, Khargone district, died with hind-limb paralysis; dehydration and starvation suspected. Officials say food-water availability and health monitoring are under review; the body was cremated per protocol.

triage.headline_ja: 森の中で『プリンス』が謎の死を遂げる！体に外傷なく、胃にも食べ物なし…獰猛な動物を病気にしているのは何か？
triage.triage_reason: 野生のトラの原因不明死（短期間に2件目）であり、感染症の可能性が示唆されているが、検査結果待ちでヒトへの影響は不明なため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 野生トラの死因は感染症の可能性があるが検査結果待ちであり、人獣共通感染症としての確証はない。同地域で短期間に2頭目のトラの原因不明死が発生しており、野生動物の健康モニタリングとして注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Pilibhit News: Risk of diseases in low-lying areas due to waterlogging.
article.articleSummary: Bisalpur, Pilibhit: Despite crores spent by the municipality to build large drains to curb chronic waterlogging, several city areas still hold floodwater. Water scarcely drains, leaving homes inundated in many colonies and main roads flooded, hindering movement. Even after the monsoon ends, water remains in lower-lying areas, including posh colonies and mohallas, forming stagnant pools. This elevates the risk of dengue and malaria as pathogens proliferate in stagnant water. Officials are attempting to fix drainage and mitigate health risks, but residents continue to face waterlogged streets and potential vector-borne disease outbreaks.

triage.headline_ja: ピリービート:排水不良により低地で疾病リスク
triage.triage_reason: 特定の症例報告ではなく、排水不良による一般的なデング・マラリアリスクの懸念を伝える内容であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準のいずれにも明確に該当しない。
triage.notes: 具体的な症例数や死亡者数の報告はなく、排水インフラ問題による将来的な媒介動物感染症リスクの懸念を伝える一般的な地方記事。

article.articleHeadline: Mother infected with Hepatitis B, 90% of newborns may become chronically infected.
article.articleSummary: In Hung Yen, a 32-year-old pregnant woman at 34 weeks with chronic hepatitis B (HBV) presented with fatigue, progressive jaundice, and dark urine; she was admitted to Bach Mai Hospital and found to have advanced HBV with coagulopathy (prothrombin activity ~57%). Her husband also has HBV. This case illustrates the high risk of mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) during late pregnancy, and the potential for newborns infected at birth to develop chronic infection in 85–90% of cases. Poor maternal monitoring may mask disease progression. WHO and CDC note that chronic HBV risk is strongly age-dependent, being much higher for perinatal transmission. Preventive strategy recommended includes antenatal HBV screening, viral load assessment, antiviral therapy when indicated, and newborn prophylaxis with hepatitis B vaccine plus hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) per guidelines. Globally, about 240 million live with chronic HBV, causing roughly 1.1 million deaths.

triage.headline_ja: B型肝炎に感染した母親、新生児の90%が慢性疾患の患者になる可能性
triage.triage_reason: 個別症例に基づく母子感染リスクの啓発記事であり、公衆衛生上の異常発生や急性のアウトブレイクを示すものではない。
triage.notes: 既知の慢性感染症（B型肝炎）に関する個別症例報告・啓発記事であり、アウトブレイクや異常事象ではないためDISMISS。発生地域にVietnamが記載されているが、個別症例であり国としての公衆衛生イベントではないためverified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: 17 defendants were sentenced in the case of pork meat infected with African swine fever at Ha Long Canned Foods Company.
article.articleSummary: Seventeen defendants in Haiphong were sentenced in a case involving African swine fever (ASF)-infected pork used by Ha Long Canned Foods Company. On Sept 30, 2026, the Hai Phong City People’s Court convicted 15 defendants of food safety violations tied to importing and processing ASF-infected pork from supplier Bui Duc Trong. Former company CEO Truong Sy Toan received 19 years; Trong 18 years; other defendants faced 3 to 16 years. In separate bribery-related charges, Le Nhat Huy received 18 months and Tran Thi Huong four years. The court found that Toan, deputy quality-control head Pham Thi Thuy Lan, lead quality inspector Bui Thi Thoan, and incoming-material handler Lai Thi Thanh Huong bypassed testing, allowing over 197 metric tons of ASF-infected pork from May 2025 through Sept 8, 2025 to be used in production. The total value of violative meat was about 17.4 billion VND, with over 9.7 billion VND destroyed.

triage.headline_ja: ハロン缶詰会社でのアフリカ豚コレラ感染豚肉事件、被告17人に判決
triage.triage_reason: アフリカ豚熱(ASF)はヒトに感染しない動物疾病であり、本記事は2025年の事件に対する司法判決についての報道で、新規の公衆衛生上の脅威やアウトブレイクを示すものではない。
triage.notes: ASFは家畜(豚)の疾病でありヒト感染症ではないため、ヒトの公衆衛生リスクとしての評価対象外。記事内容は食品安全法違反に関する刑事裁判の結果報道。

article.articleHeadline: Taking turns off from work to care for a child with recurrent hand-foot-mouth disease.
article.articleSummary: Ho Chi Minh City recorded 1,283 HFMD cases in Sep 14–20, up 47% from the prior four weeks; cases reached 35,121 by week 38. Tom, 18 months, had HFMD twice in one month: first Coxsackievirus A16, then Enterovirus 71 (EV71) a week later (grade 1). EV71 can cause neurological, cardiac, and respiratory complications; caregivers were advised to monitor at home and seek hospital care for persistent high fever, tremors, or poor intake. Tom’s third infection occurred on Oct 2 after returning to nursery; his parents split duties, taking unpaid leave and incurring reduced income. HFMD spreads via fecal-oral, droplets, and contaminated surfaces, with daycare as a high-risk setting. EV71 vaccine, approved by Health Ministry, began rollout at VNVC on Sep 25; about 300 centers have administered about 30,000 doses to children 2 months to under 6 years, 2–3 doses. The vaccine targets EV71 and does not protect against Coxsackievirus A16.

triage.headline_ja: 交代で休みを取り、手足口病を繰り返す子どもの看病をする
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム・ホーチミン市で手足口病（EV71含む）の症例が増加しているが、季節性の既知の感染症であり、重症化・国際的拡大の明確な証拠はないため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 手足口病はベトナムで季節性に流行する既知の感染症。EV71による重症化リスクはあるが、本記事の症例はグレード1で軽症。ワクチン接種が既に開始されており、保健省主導で対応が進んでいる。

article.articleHeadline: Gia Lai monitors exposed individuals after identification of a melioidosis case.
article.articleSummary: Melioidosis (Burkholderia pseudomallei) case identified in Gia Lai Province, Vietnam. A 47-year-old male farmer from Ple Oi hamlet, Chư A Thai commune, developed fever, rigors, cough, dyspnea and chest pain on 7 Sept after injuring his left thumb washing a rainwater barrel. Blood culture on 23 Sept confirmed Burkholderia pseudomallei; diagnosis: septicemia due to melioidosis. He was transferred to Gia Lai General Hospital on 24 Sept; condition stable at reporting. Epidemiology linked exposure to farming with overnight stays in a shack in a rubber garden near the Chu Se Pass, 4 km from home; frequent contact with soil, mud and rainwater without boots or gloves; damp with two stagnant pools. Interventions included Chloramin B disinfection, water treatment, removal of standing water, and health education. Exposed contacts monitored for 21 days; no additional cases detected. Authorities urge protective gear for those in soil/water and prompt reporting of fever, pneumonia or abscess.

article.articleHeadline: The plague has resurfaced in Russia. It began with a young lab technician.
article.articleSummary: Plague has resurfaced in Russia, starting with a 27-year-old institute employee who died from Yersinia pestis. Twelve of 189 people were placed under observation at a plague treatment facility as authorities trace contacts. Two exposure scenarios: contact with bacteria in a broken diagnostic test tube, or infection during travel to Buryatia border with Mongolia, where an outbreak was detected. Authorities, including Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobziew, convened an emergency commission. Plague has three forms—bubonic, septicemic, and pneumonic—with initial symptoms appearing 2–7 days after exposure: fever, chills, severe headache, muscle pain, and weakness; bubonic plague causes painful lymph node swelling. Prompt treatment requires potent antibiotics. Historically deadly, the disease killed millions in the medieval era. Last Russian case was in 2016 in Altai. Ongoing foci persist in Madagascar, DRC, Algeria, China, Vietnam, and Mongolia; Mongolia reported 137 foci in 2023 near the Russian border. Poland has been plague-free for over 300 years.

article.articleHeadline: Warning: High-Risk Individuals May Contract Infectious Diseases.
article.articleSummary: By 2030, Vietnam will have about 18 million people aged 60+, with roughly two-thirds having chronic conditions and over half with multiple diseases. About 95% of older adults will have at least one chronic disease, averaging 2–3 conditions—most commonly cardiovascular disease, diabetes, musculoskeletal disorders, or cognitive decline—leading to roughly a decade living with illness. This burden elevates healthcare costs and pressures facilities. Diabetes and chronic kidney disease can weaken immunity; diabetics face higher rates of respiratory infections and pneumonia, with a 38% higher risk of herpes zoster and greater risk of severe RSV in the elderly. CKD increases herpes zoster risk by ~29% and RSV risk/progression. At the Vietnamese Association of Urology–Nephrology conference (VUNA), experts urged vaccination as proactive prevention, echoing KDIGO 2024 CKD guidance and MoH’s 2026 decision endorsing vaccines (HBV, HPV, RSV, influenza, pneumococcus, shingles). Integrated care, combining treatment and prevention, is emphasized, with GSK Vietnam collaboration.

article.articleHeadline: Moringa Shows Promise Against Bacteria Infections and Inflammation
article.articleSummary: 2026-10-02: A review of Moringa oleifera leaves and stems (134 references from PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar) reports antibacterial and anti-inflammatory potential. Lab studies show activity against Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Enterococcus faecalis, with leaf/stem MICs roughly 0.2–4 mg/mL. Mechanisms include bacterial membrane damage, enzyme interference, reduced adhesion, disrupted quorum sensing, and biofilm inhibition. Astragalin (IC50 ~0.22 mg/mL against E. coli) and compounds such as rutin, chlorogenic acid, and hyperoside contribute activity; astragalin also reduces adhesion and biofilm integrity. On the inflammatory side, Moringin (isothiocyanate) may activate the Nrf2/Keap1 pathway and inhibit NF-κB, while quercetin and kaempferol may lower cytokines and COX/LOX activity. In rats with infected diabetic ulcers, leaf extract reduced bacterial burden and proinflammatory TNF-α/IL-1β, increased anti-inflammatory IL-10, and sped up wound closure, though synergy is unproven. Human evidence is limited; no large randomized trials exist, underscoring the need for standardized preparations and robust clinical studies. Published in International Journal of Molecular Sciences; Thailand Medical News highlighted the findings.

article.articleHeadline: Baden-Württemberg: Sindbis Fever in Germany — What You Need to Know.
article.articleSummary: Germany reports its first locally acquired Sindbis virus (SINV) infection. A 60-year-old man from Baden-Württemberg fell ill on 12 July; SINV was confirmed in September after chikungunya testing due to exposure to Asian tiger mosquitoes (Aedes albopictus). SINV circulates mainly among birds and is transmitted by mosquitoes; there is no human-to-human transmission. Most infections are mild or asymptomatic; when symptomatic, fever, itchy rash, and joint pain occur, with arthritis persisting for months in some. Overall risk is low; no specific high-risk group is identified. No targeted therapy exists; treatment is supportive with analgesics and anti-inflammatory drugs. Prevention follows general mosquito protection. SINV is found across Eurasia and Africa; Europe has had detections in Finland and Sweden, with Germany previously reporting SINV in mosquitoes (Weinheim, 2009). Clinicians should consider SINV in patients with fever, rash, and arthralgia during mosquito season, even without travel, and test after negative dengue/chikungunya results.

article.articleHeadline: Deadly virus found in ancient Gospels — it has been killing for 3,700 years.
article.articleSummary: DNA of the sheep pox virus was found on parchment from York Gospels, produced by Anglo-Saxon scribes in Canterbury in the late 10th century and later at York Minster. Parchment came from skins of sheep, goats, and calves, and molecular analysis detected traces on sheep parchment as well as on calf- and goat-skin pages, suggesting transmission through mixed livestock keeping or during hide processing. Researchers compared the viral DNA with material from Bronze Age sheep teeth and recovered 21 viral genomes; earliest samples date to about 1700 BCE. Data show that sheep pox circulated among Eurasian livestock for over 3,700 years, and the viral genome remained remarkably stable over the last 3.5 millennia, with key host-adapting changes arising before this period. Sheep pox remains a serious threat to livestock today; ancient genomes aid understanding of evolution and may inform new control methods. Archives may hold further traces of infections worldwide.

article.articleHeadline: Palawan confirms ASF case, strengthen containment measures
article.articleSummary: Palawan Province confirms its first African Swine Fever (ASF) case in Barangay Concepcion, Agutaya, with Bureau of Animal Industry lab confirming ASF in 40 Concepcion samples. Quarantine checkpoints are in place across Agutaya to restrict movement of people, animals, and materials. A three-day depopulation operation (Sept 28–30) targeted remaining hogs to break transmission. DA-MIMAROPA provides disinfectants, rapid test kits, depopulation guidance, indemnification procedures, movement controls, biosecurity, and disease surveillance support. Active surveillance, field investigations, and sample collection are ongoing to detect hidden cases in Agutaya. The province is recording hog-raiser losses and arranging aid. Information campaigns urge raisers to limit pig movements, disinfect gear, report sudden illness or death, and avoid transporting or slaughtering suspected pigs or meat without veterinary guidance. ASF does not infect humans; spread occurs via contaminated pork, equipment, vehicles, footwear, and other materials; cooperation with quarantine personnel is essential.

article.articleHeadline: PH recognizes Hungary bird flu zoning, keeps poultry trade
article.articleSummary: PH grants Hungary bilateral recognition of its HPAI status, ensuring continued poultry trade as of 2026-10-02. Hungary will export only from regions free of high-path avian influenza, under regionalization terms (Administrative Circular No. 09) and current DA regulations. Exporters can secure bilateral recognition to protect food security amid rising poultry demand. The circular notes that whole-country bans limit sources of day-old chicks, parent stocks, and poultry meat, driving up prices. Hungary's application for regionalization was reviewed by the Bureau of Animal Industry, which concluded the country maintains sufficient veterinary oversight and control measures against HPAI. This recognition lowers import risk from designated zones. Hungary exported 5,000 kilograms of meat to the Philippines from January to August, per BAI data; in 2025, shipments reached 67,574 kg.

article.articleHeadline: Rabies management
article.articleSummary: Rabies management in Brazil emphasizes prevention, as rabies has no cure. After a bite from a dog thought to be mad, urgent vaccination and, if indicated, rabies immunoglobulin, are necessary. If a dog is known, it can be observed for up to 10 days. If the dog stays healthy for ten days, vaccination is not needed; if it develops illness or disappears, post-exposure vaccination is warranted. Symptoms of rabies in humans include malaise and hydrophobia (inability to swallow water). The piece also uses a social analogy to emphasize controlling anger, but the medical guidance remains. Post-exposure vaccines and rabies serum, when needed, are available in Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS); in the private sector, they are not available. The date provided is 2026-10-02.

MPF will monitor to inform public health measures.

article.articleHeadline: Where there are more cats, there is higher well-being — but Toxoplasma casts a shadow over the picture.
article.articleSummary: On Oct 2, 2026, a study by a Mexican team analyzed data from 93 countries to examine links between cat ownership, Toxoplasma gondii, and national well-being. They found a positive association between domestic cat density per 10,000 people and well-being; Finland, Denmark, and Sweden had both high cat density (about 1,700–2,000 cats per 10,000 people) and high well-being. By contrast, prevalence of Toxoplasma gondii tended to align with lower well-being, especially in Lebanon, Yemen, Gabon, and Ethiopia. Saudi Arabia and Brazil were exceptions: high toxoplasma prevalence but relatively favorable well-being. The researchers stress the findings are correlational, not causal, and confounding factors such as income and healthcare could influence both pet ownership and well-being. Notably, more cats did not correspond to higher toxoplasma rates, underscoring a complex relationship among animals, pathogens, and society.

article.articleHeadline: Blood donation has new rules in Brazil; see age, timeframes, and malaria test.
article.articleSummary: Brazil implemented nationwide blood donation reforms under Portaria GM/MS 11.685/2026, taking effect Oct 30, 2026. Regular donors with a history of voluntary donation may continue past age 70 if healthy and medically cleared; first-time donors must be under 60 to later donate in the 60–69 bracket. Adolescents 16+ may apply with a guardian’s authorization. Deferral periods for tattoos, permanent makeup, certain cosmetic procedures, and piercings are adjusted: seven days if sanitary conditions can be verified, otherwise four months; mouth or genital piercings require four months after removal. Endoscopy and non-prescription anabolic steroids deferrals reduce from six to four months. Malaria testing becomes mandatory in all screening; the NAT Plus assay now detects malaria in addition to HIV and hepatitis B/C, shortening malaria-exposure deferral to 30 days. Blood bag and sample labeling adopt ISBT 128 to improve traceability. Platelet concentrates may be stored up to seven days.

article.articleHeadline: Cutaneous Larva Migrans: Learn How Transmission Occurs, What the Symptoms Are, and How to Prevent
article.articleSummary: Cutaneous larva migrans (creeping eruption) is caused by hookworm larvae penetrating the skin after contact with soil or sand contaminated with animal feces, typically at beaches, parks, or areas frequented by dogs and cats. Transmission occurs via direct skin contact with contaminated ground; insect bites do not transmit the infection. The larvae migrate within the epidermis, producing red, serpiginous tracks that resemble a map and may advance about 1 cm per day. Intense itching, often worse at night, along with redness, swelling, and inflammation along the tract are characteristic. Although larvae may die spontaneously after weeks, symptoms can be burdensome and lead to medical care. Treatments include antiparasitic drugs such as thiabendazole, albendazole, or ivermectin, administered topically or orally depending on extent. Prevention centers on wearing footwear, avoiding direct contact with contaminated sand or soil, deworming pets, and promptly cleaning up pet feces; do not attempt self-removal of larvae.

article.articleHeadline: Private sector guarantees availability of yellow fever vaccine for travelers.
article.articleSummary: Yellow fever vaccine supply is guaranteed in the private sector for travelers from Costa Rica after a new travel-health rule took effect Oct 1, 2026. Costa Rican travelers heading to Bolivia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Venezuela, Colombia, Brazil, Peru, and several African nations must be vaccinated against yellow fever to enter; the shot must be administered at least 10 days before departure, and travelers must carry the international vaccination certificate. Private pharmacies and vaccination centers report adequate stock, with doses priced roughly between 60,000 and 80,000 Costa Rican colón. The CCSS also offers vaccination, subject to appointment availability and possession of a flight ticket to risk destinations. Digital vaccination certificates are accessible via the Ministry of Health Virtual Office, the EDUS app, and the Pura Vida Móvil platform. Massimo Manzi of the Chamber of Health affirmed sufficient private-dose supply.

article.articleHeadline: Campinas has more than 30 neighborhoods at higher risk of dengue; see the list - Portal Veloz.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever in Campinas, Brazil: As of Sep 28, 2026, Campinas reports 4,053 confirmed dengue cases this year, with no deaths. The 40th Alerta Arboviroses Campinas (Oct 1) designates 32 bairros as higher transmission risk in the last week, by region: East — Vila Itapura, Vila 31 de Março, Vila Lafayette Álvaro, Parque Brasília, Jardim Flamboyant, Vila Nogueira; Northwest — Vila Padre Manoel de Nóbrega, Jardim Garcia, Conjunto Parque São Bento, Parque da Floresta, Cidade Satélite Íris I; North — Bonfim, Botafogo, Vila Proost de Souza, Jardim Chapadão; Southwest — Porto Seguro, Vida Nova, Vila Vitória, DIC V and DIC VI, Jardim Melina, Jardim Aeronave de Viracopos; South — Jardim Puccamp, Jardim Columbia, Jardim San Diego, Parque das Camélias, Jardim Mercedes, Vila Abaeté; Southeast — Parque Jambeiro, Jardim Santa Judith, Jardim Leonor, Ponte Preta. From Jan 1 to Sep 23, 2026, health teams conducted 1,270,445 home visits for breeding-site control and 53,382 outdoor nebulizations to curb Aedes aegypti. Community participation is essential; 80% of breeding sites are inside homes. Recommendations include eliminating standing water, refreshing plant water every two days, cleaning plant saucers weekly, and sealing unused water tanks.

article.articleHeadline: In a drier world, some infectious diseases are unexpectedly thriving
article.articleSummary: New research synthesized nearly 100 studies to show that drier conditions, driven by warming, can intensify some infectious diseases while suppressing others. The drought-disease paradox notes that water scarcity often concentrates hosts and vectors at remaining water sources, boosting transmission. In California, droughts contributed to thousands of valley fever cases, and a 2014 drought correlated with West Nile virus spikes; a 2017 Somalia drought led to about 80,000 cholera cases and over 1,000 deaths. In Brazil, dengue risk rises in the months after drought. By contrast, prolonged drought can curb certain pathogens, or alter water chemistry to be hostile (hotter, saltier, low oxygen), and even eliminate organisms like Vibrio vulnificus after long droughts. Globally, about 77% of land is drier than 30 years ago. The study highlights the role of animal movements around shrinking water sources in shaping outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: October 2, 2026 - Lauro de Freitas trains professionals to strengthen diagnosis and treatment of Hansen's disease and Sporotrichosis.
article.articleSummary: On October 2, 2026, Lauro de Freitas’ Municipal Health Secretariat (SESA) hosted a briefing for health professionals at UNIME to strengthen diagnosis and treatment of Hansen's disease (leprosy) and Sporotrichosis. The session targeted physicians, nurses, and other network staff, emphasizing early detection, appropriate clinical management, and reinforced epidemiological surveillance to curb transmission in Lauro de Freitas, Brazil. Experts covered practical aspects of Hansen's disease — a chronic infectious condition affecting skin and peripheral nerves — and Sporotrichosis, a deep fungal infection often linked to contact with infected animals, stressing timely identification and correct treatment. Lucas Carvalho Meira, Director of Epidemiological Surveillance, underscored the program's strategic value for rapid response. Andrea Rebouças led the training, outlining referral workflows, while pharmacist Rosa Cruz noted aligning community pharmacy guidance with new guidelines to support treatment.

article.articleHeadline: Influencer is hospitalized after an infection returns with severe pain and vomiting.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-10-02, Brazilian digital influencer Jéssica Ingrede from Acre was hospitalized in the capital after a previously contracted infection resurfaced. The illness originated during a trip to Cruzeiro do Sul, in interior Acre. The return of the infection caused severe vomiting, nausea, and intense pain. She initially sought care at an urgent care clinic, but symptoms worsened, requiring admission to a private hospital. At the hospital, she underwent an electrocardiogram and comprehensive testing; she endured extreme pain necessitating morphine. In Cruzeiro do Sul she reportedly had only malaise and no tests, but at the current facility many abnormal laboratory values were detected, prompting inpatient care. She remains under observation with some fluctuations in condition but reports improvement and emphasizes adhering to the prescribed treatment. The case highlights a reemergence of infection after an initial period of recovery.

article.articleHeadline: Famato reinforces precautions to prevent rabies and alerts to the importance of reporting suspected cases in herds
article.articleSummary: Six rabies cases were confirmed in September in Mato Grosso: one equine and five bovines on farms in Dom Aquino and Rondonópolis. Mato Grosso reported 25 foci in 2024, 26 in 2025, and 18 foci through September 27, 2026. Famato emphasizes vaccination and reporting to Indea-MT for investigation by the Official Veterinary Service. Rabies is a fatal viral disease of the central nervous system, mainly transmitted to production animals by hematophagous bats. Neurologic signs include herd isolation, ataxia, stumbling, hind-limb paralysis, urinary/defecatory issues, and death after lateral recumbency with paddling. Early reporting allows lab confirmation by Indea’s own lab, in partnership with UFMT, at no cost to producers. Humans are at risk; seek care and inform Indea-MT after bat exposure. Vaccination: initial two-dose schedule 30 days apart for newcomers, then annual boosters; avoid handling suspect animals and refrain from capturing bats.

article.articleHeadline: Leishmaniasis is the topic of a lecture for health professionals from Felisburgo and Rio do Prado
article.articleSummary: Health professionals from Felisburgo and Rio do Prado in Brazil attended a lecture on leishmaniasis, held as a collaboration between the Felisburgo and Rio do Prado city halls and the Nascentes de Pureza Masonic Lodge. The session focused on recognizing the disease's main symptoms, preventive measures, and the importance of seeking medical care for suspected cases. The aim was to strengthen local capacity to identify possible infections and implement prevention strategies. Participants were reminded to monitor for signs warranting professional evaluation, such as non-healing wounds that persist. Leishmaniasis is an infectious disease caused by Leishmania parasites and transmitted by phlebotomine sandflies. Early detection and appropriate treatment depend on prompt medical consultation. The initiative underscores ongoing training of health teams and information dissemination to protect the population from leishmaniasis.

article.articleHeadline: Ecuador reports an increase in dengue cases ahead of El Niño's arrival.
article.articleSummary: Dengue cases rise in Ecuador ahead of El Niño. From Aug 31 to Sep 6, 2026, the Ministry of Public Health reports 34,058 dengue infections nationwide, an 18% increase from the same period in 2025, with an incidence of about 172 per 100,000 population. The highest burden is in Guayas province, with deaths in Naranjal, Balzar, Durán, and Salitre. In Guayaquil, by Sep 22, 2026, 459 dengue cases have been reported citywide, including 47 in September; August had 57 cases, a 17.5% decline. Dengue is categorized as without warning signs, with warning signs, and severe dengue; in Guayaquil most cases lack warning signs. Common symptoms include fever >38°C, headache, myalgias, and malaise. Warning signs include persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, and mucosal bleeding. Illness typically lasts 1–7 days (up to 10). Authorities warn against self-medication and NSAID misuse; prevention emphasizes reducing Aedes mosquito breeding.

article.articleHeadline: Guyana leads Amazon health cooperation talks on malaria elimination, Indigenous health - INews Guyana
article.articleSummary: Malaria elimination drives Amazon regional talks as Guyana, presiding over CESAM, convenes Amazon countries (Guyana, Bolivia, Suriname, Venezuela in person; Brazil virtually) to advance malaria control, Indigenous health, and surveillance. The meeting, since Sept 8, 2026, identified malaria, hepatitis B and C, Indigenous health, intercultural health, and surveillance as priorities. Suriname shared success eliminating local malaria transmission through community-based diagnosis and rapid response; ACTO proposed a technical workshop in Suriname to share practices. Bolivia highlighted Indigenous health access challenges and mercury contamination from gold mining. Brazil reaffirmed cooperation on Indigenous health; Venezuela urged culturally appropriate care and stronger joint surveillance for malaria, dengue, and onchocerciasis. PAHO pledged technical cooperation, linking elimination to culturally appropriate approaches. A health module for the Amazon Regional Observatory and national focal points for data exchange were discussed. Malaria remains a top priority; hepatitis cooperation to continue with multilateral financing.

article.articleHeadline: Tuberculosis cases are increasing in Imperatriz; the municipality has already recorded 150 notifications in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Imperatriz, Maranhão, Brazil, recorded 150 tuberculosis notifications in 2026, with 103 cases among city residents. In 2024 there were 166 total cases (122 residents); 2025 saw 229 (162 residents). Officials attribute fluctuations to underreporting rather than a sharp surge. The Municipal Tuberculosis Program coordinator, Menildes Paixão, emphasizes early diagnosis to improve treatment and prevent lasting sequelae. Infectious disease specialist Aldicléya Luz notes that persistent symptoms should prompt evaluation; key signs include a cough lasting at least three weeks, fever, weight loss, coughing up blood, and night sweats. Data come from Semus (Municipal Health Secretariat). The article underscores ongoing TB activity and urges residents with symptoms to seek medical assessment to enable timely diagnosis and management.

article.articleHeadline: New research: Climate, floods and waterborne disease in Myanmar | MIMU
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-02, an open-access study of Myanmar (2021–2025) links waterborne disease to climate data and water–health policy context. The analysis combines health records with climate variables and a policy review, finding that cholera and acute watery diarrhoea cases peak in the rainy season, with coastal and delta areas such as Rakhine and Ayeyarwady reporting the most cholera. Fatality rates are higher in conflict-affected areas with weak infrastructure. Flooding shows association with outbreaks, but temperature and rainfall alone do not explain the patterns. The authors conclude that access to clean water and sanitation matters more than climate events by themselves and urge better cross-sector coordination between water and health, stronger data sharing, expanded local WASH services, and climate-resilient planning. Published in Water Research X (open access).

article.articleHeadline: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention introduction is associated with sustained reductions in childhood malaria burden in northern Ghana
article.articleSummary: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) was introduced in Ghana’s Northern Region in June 2019, delivering monthly sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine to children aged 3–59 months during the June–September rainy season. Analyzing 10 years of monthly health facility data (2015–2024) and four rounds of national household surveys (2014–2022) with seasonal ARIMA and Bayesian structural time-series methods, post-SMC outcomes were lower than the counterfactual: malaria deaths (−80.3%), admissions (−23.0%), and incidence (−16.1%). At the individual level, post-SMC children had significantly lower odds of malaria infection (adjusted OR 0.595; 95% CI 0.470–0.751). Despite a decline in insecticide-treated net coverage, malaria burden continued to fall across data sources. The findings suggest an association between SMC implementation and reduced childhood malaria burden in this high-transmission Sahelian setting, underscoring the need to maintain high SMC coverage as part of integrated malaria control in northern Ghana.

article.articleHeadline: Herbal Remedies Remain First Response to Childhood Malaria in Ghana's
article.articleSummary: Tamale Metropolis, northern Ghana, reports malaria as a persistent threat to children. A cross-sectional study of 265 female caregivers of children ≤12 found 37.3% used plant-based medicines as first-line treatment for suspected malaria. Despite broad access to artemisinin-based combination therapies via hospitals, clinics, and licensed sellers, herbal remedies remain common; fever and vomiting were the main triggers for suspecting malaria, and 77.6% would first seek hospital care, indicating parallel use of formal care and herbal practice. Frequently cited plants: Azadirachta indica (neem) 18.7%, Carica papaya 16.5%, Psidium guajava (guava) 14.3%, Senna occidentalis 10%, Mangifera indica (mango) 9.6%. The study highlights practice vs. efficacy concerns, potential delays in accurate diagnosis, and possible herb–drug interactions. Low-income caregivers had markedly higher odds of herbal first-line use (adjusted OR 9.449; 95% CI 1.185–75.354). Published 2026-10-02 in BMC Complementary Medicine and Therapies.
